clue.text: Spies hidden office

parts.note: something hidden is kept secret
an office is a religious service, as in the divine office

explanation.surface: Agents conceal a government bureau.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligence agency staffed by agents is collectively called by this name, so it stands for spies as a body.

clue.text: Favourite place for having tantrums?

parts.note: a much-frequented haunt, read literally as the ground where a child stamps its feet in a rage

explanation.surface: Where does a toddler prefer to throw fits?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a regular haunt, while literally a tantrum involves stamping on the floor.

clue.text: Getting this increases don's standing, oddly

definitions.text: Getting this increases don's standing, oddly

parts.words: Getting this increases don's standing, oddly
parts.note: a university lecturer gains status by being appointed professor, odd since the seat in question is for sitting

explanation.surface: A lecturer's promotion raises their status, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called by the name of a seat, so earning one raises a don's rank though it is something to sit on.

clue.text: For instance, new concerti ignoring others

parts.note: for instance is abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of concerti are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh set of concertos shows no regard for anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CONCERTI as OCENTRIC; 'For instance' looks like a link but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person thinks only of themself and pays no heed to anyone else.

clue.text: Such a good type isn't commonly involved in cunning

indicators.note: involved in means placed within the word for cunning, wrapped by it

parts.note: cunning means sly
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A virtuous person isn't usually caught up in trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is the model of a good person, and the adjective describes someone of that kind.

clue.text: Channel needs good sailors like these

definitions.meaning: a television channel needs high audience figures
ordinary seamen in the navy below officer rank

explanation.surface: Crossing the English Channel calls for capable seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the sea Channel; it is a TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewing figures and non-commissioned naval seamen share this one word.

clue.text: Centre for missionaries

indicators.note: centre for means the letters are taken from the middle of the word missionaries

explanation.surface: A base for people spreading their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: IONA is the Scottish island where St Columba founded a monastery in 563 that sent monks out to convert the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The island was the base from which Columba's monks evangelised Scotland and northern England.

clue.text: Transport carrying bishop goes into plant

indicators.note: carrying means the word for transport holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a transport is a fit of ecstasy, euphoria
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A vehicle with a cleric on board crashes into some greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like a vehicle but means rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurges are the genus of flowering plants known by this botanical name.

clue.text: Mad Hatter fled rage king displayed

indicators.note: mad signals that the following letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's crazed hatmaker storms off in fury before the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ALFRED THE GREAT was the ninth-century king of Wessex.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a ruler of the West Saxons, one of England's most celebrated monarchs.

clue.text: One prepared to analyze anybody in title role

definitions.text: One prepared to analyze anybody in title role

parts.words: One prepared to analyze anybody in title role
parts.note: someone who dissects any body, and also the lead character of a James Bridie play named after that profession

explanation.surface: An actor ready to psychoanalyse anyone while playing the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anybody' splits as 'any body'; The Anatomist is a 1930 play by James Bridie.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissector of bodies studies their structure, and Bridie's play takes its title from that profession.

clue.text: The state of penal reform

indicators.note: reform means the letters of penal are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: The condition of prison reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan country is a sovereign nation, a state in the political sense.

clue.text: Bag's become wrinkled

definitions.meaning: a small bag for money, a handbag
to pucker, as lips do when drawn together

explanation.surface: A sack has gone creased.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a money pouch and to gather into tight folds like pursed lips.

clue.text: Accent from the South-West?

parts.note: a word for vocal inflection that is also the name of a river in Somerset

explanation.surface: A West Country way of speaking?
explanation.walkthrough: The Tone is a river through Taunton in Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone is a manner of voice, an accent, and also the name of a south-western river.

clue.text: 28 includes two of this crew

parts.note: the answer to 28 contains the word for a rowing eight, which can be split into two smaller rowing boats

explanation.surface: A number that contains two teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is PIECES OF EIGHT; an eight in rowing holds two crews of the size wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat with this many oarsmen is half an eight.

clue.text: Chart showing relative positions

parts.note: a diagram placing kin by their relationships, relative meaning a family member

explanation.surface: A diagram of where things stand compared with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical diagram shows where each family member sits in relation to the others.

clue.text: Regularly late? Sounds chivalrous, however

indicators.note: sounds means the word for chivalrous is said aloud, giving a word of identical pronunciation

parts.note: chivalrous behaviour befits a knight, so knightly

explanation.surface: Always behind time? That seems gallant, though.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every evening happens regularly at a late hour.

clue.text: Bird set out on part of flight in March

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a goose is a bird
a step is one part of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A bird set off on a stage of its migration in March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests the bird flying; it is a flight of stairs. 'set out' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff-legged military parade gait is a kind of march.

clue.text: Injured fliers returned to base

indicators.note: returned means the word for fliers comes back the other way

parts.note: bats are flying mammals
a bed is a base, as a riverbed or flowerbed

explanation.surface: Wounded birds flew home to their headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierced with a knife, a person has been wounded.

clue.text: Upstart out of place in group is architect

indicators.note: out of place means a letter is moved from its proper position within the group of letters

parts.note: the start of Up is U

explanation.surface: A social climber who doesn't fit in the set is a designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' moves the U of GROUPIS along two spaces. Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Gropius was the German founder of the Bauhaus school of design and building.

clue.text: Country divided by Trade Union legislation

indicators.note: divided by means the country word is split with the union letters set inside

parts.note: a country is a state

explanation.surface: A nation split by organised labour over a new law.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act of Parliament is a written law, a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Twist head off each vegetable

parts.note: to twist is to spin

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of each is cut away

explanation.surface: Wring the top off every vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy green eaten cooked or raw is a common vegetable.

clue.text: Broadcast. — and needle, we hear, unnamed person

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said aloud and their sounds give the letters entered

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it; taken as written; to needle is to stitch, sew

explanation.surface: Scatter seed and stitch, as it sounds, for someone not named.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands in for a person whose name is not given.

clue.text: First river out of line? European one

indicators.note: out of means the letter is taken away from the word for line

parts.note: a line or row of things is an order, as in order of battle

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of river

explanation.surface: Is the first river out of line? A continental one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is a European river forming part of the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder flows through central Europe, so it is one continental river.

clue.text: Miss a sporting occasion

parts.note: a miss is a girl, a gal

explanation.surface: Fail to attend an athletics meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming gala is a sports competition, a festive event.

clue.text: Religious leader unlikely to be elder

definitions.meaning: Brigham ... led the Mormon church to Utah
a youthful person is not the senior one

explanation.surface: A churchman not likely to be the senior one.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigham Young was the second president of the Mormon church; 'elder' is also a Mormon title.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigham Young was a famous Mormon leader, and the word also means not old.

clue.text: What's employer doing to make union leader whistle?

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of union

parts.note: to whistle or sing is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: What makes a boss get the union chief to blow the whistle?
explanation.walkthrough: An employer is a user, so what a user does is this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a thing puts it to work, so is engaged in this activity.

clue.text: Mule, for example — soundly beat it!

indicators.note: soundly means the phrase is said aloud and spelt as a word of the same sound

parts.note: shoo is a command to go away, beat it

explanation.surface: Thrash a stubborn animal!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mule' looks like the animal, which 'beat it' plays up; a mule is a backless slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a backless slip-on piece of footwear, one kind of the item.

clue.text: Score team's opening century, in dramatic form

indicators.note: in means the letters are placed inside the theatre word

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese theatre

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of team's

explanation.surface: A side's first hundred, scored in theatrical fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'century' suggest cricket; score means a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to make a cut or groove, a nick.

clue.text: Emphasize it's less than 14

parts.note: less than means under
14 is FAMILY TREE, a line of descent

explanation.surface: Stress that something is below a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to draw a rule beneath it, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Two-and-six, perhaps, in old money

parts.note: two and six are parts of the number eight, and old Spanish silver dollars had that name

explanation.surface: Half a crown in pre-decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Two-and-six (two shillings and sixpence) was a British pre-decimal sum, but the clue means 2 and 6 as portions of 8.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish silver dollars of pirate lore bore this name, and two and six are fractions that add to eight.
